details.description: Nova-2 General is Deepgram's general-purpose speech-to-text model in its Nova-2 tier, described by Deepgram's docs as optimized for everyday audio processing. It expands on the earlier Nova-1 model with speech-specific Transformer optimizations, additional data curation, and multi-stage training, which Deepgram says reduce word error rate and improve entity recognition, punctuation, and capitalization compared with Nova-1. It supports about 35 languages, including Spanish-English code-switching. Deepgram's current models overview table recommends its newer Nova-3 tier as the default general-purpose choice, and now positions Nova-2 mainly for languages Nova-3 does not yet support and for filler-word identification.
advantages: Supports about 35 languages, including multilingual Spanish+English code-switching in a single stream, per Deepgram's language documentation.

Deepgram says Nova-2 improves entity recognition (e.g. proper nouns, alphanumerics), punctuation, and capitalization over its Nova-1 predecessor through speech-specific Transformer optimizations, advanced data curation, and multi-stage training.
disadvantages: Deepgram's current models overview table recommends its newer Nova-3 tier, not Nova-2, as the default general-purpose ASR choice, positioning Nova-2 mainly for languages Nova-3 does not yet support and for filler-word identification.
use_cases: Everyday, general-purpose audio transcription, per Deepgram's model documentation.
Transcription in languages not yet supported by Deepgram's newer Nova-3 tier.
Filler-word identification, which Deepgram's models overview lists as a current Nova-2 use case.

notes: Deepgram's 'Nova-2 Speech-to-Text API' launch article (deepgram.com/learn/nova-2-speech-to-text-api) reports a median WER of 8.4% and other accuracy figures, but these are tested across four generic audio domains (podcast, video/media, meeting, phone call) for the Nova-2 model as a whole, not attributed to the general-tuned option specifically, so they are left out (WER is also excluded from the evaluations schema, which wants only 0-100 higher-is-better accuracy scores). Catalog facts carry no deprecation_date, consistent with Deepgram's docs, which list Nova-2 outside its 'Legacy Models' section (Nova 1, Enhanced, Base).
